chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah from 'Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding the testimony of the slave.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he is just (adl), his testimony is acceptable. Indeed, the first person to reject the testimony of a slave was 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. And that was because a slave presented himself to him regarding testimony, and he said: If I give testimony, I fear for my self; and if I conceal it, I sin against my Lord. So he said: Bring your testimony. Indeed, we do not accept the testimony of a slave after you.'
ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a slave valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the testimony of a slave is valid provided he is just ('adl), correcting the common misconception that slavery inherently invalidates legal witness. It contextualizes 'Umar ibn al-Khattab's rejection not as a permanent legal ruling, but as a specific precautionary measure due to the slave's fear of his master's retaliation, a nuance preserved by Imam al-Sadiq to distinguish between temporary practical constraints and permanent jurisprudential principles.
